primary_root_cause: Front O2 sensor or its wiring producing a persistently low signal
other_likely_causes: Unmetered air leak at the front-cylinder intake or exhaust
Low fuel delivery or a partially restricted front-cylinder injector
Exhaust leak upstream of the front O2 sensor
recommended_first_check: Inspect the front O2 sensor connector and harness for loose pins, heat damage, or chafing, then confirm the sensor signal responds to a commanded rich condition.
reasoning: P0131 is set when the ECM continues to see a low-voltage front O2 signal, which can represent either a genuinely lean front cylinder or a sensor/circuit fault. Start with the exposed sensor wiring and connector, then distinguish a failed sensor from intake, exhaust, injector, or fuel-supply causes by checking whether its voltage changes when mixture is enriched.
